title: an external project's wake reaches firstmate: every wake pushed into an external project's private queue is also forwarded, as one bounded line naming the project, onto the engine's wake queue and rung on the engine's doorbells, so a finished round, a review verdict or a card answered in the pilot external repository wakes firstmate exactly as a self event does
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05/06 no external-project event woke firstmate. the pilot external repository (project the pilot external project, store <external project path> T-002 rounds worker-pilar-t002-r1, -r2 and -r3 and reviews reviewer-daiki-t002-r1/-r2 all finished; their wake items are in <external project path> (`finished: T-002 worker-pilar-t002-r2 ok #1`, `review: T-002 APPROVE ...`), but the firstmate Stop hook never delivered one, while every self event (T-221, T-222, T-223 finished/review/CI/card) did. An external card answer (D-pilot-T001-*) on 2026-10-05 likewise never woke firstmate. Firstmate found each result only at its next 30-minute report.

Mechanism (root cause). A wake is pushed, never watched (design §11, '*Waking the harness (T-137).*', design.md:2854). `push` (bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py:565-591) appends to `os.path.join(record_root(root), WAKE_QUEUE)` and rings `ring(root, line)` (:509-516), which rings `<record_root>/state/session/wake.d`. `record_root` (bin/lib/fm_project_paths.py:119) resolves to the external project's home when FM_PROJECT names an external project (FM_EXTERNAL=1), so fm-worker.sh:364 and fm-review.sh:251 (through fm_wake_push, bin/fm-config.sh:894-897), fm-herdr.py:1964, bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:123 and bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:96 all write external wakes into the external store and ring the external store's wake.d. The board's `pushWake` (board/server.ts:1565-1578) does the same for an external card: it appends to `stateDir(project)/session/wake.jsonl` and runs `fm_lifeline.py ring` with FM_PROJECT set to that project. The firstmate watch and every other reader read only the engine's queue and doorbells: bin/lib/fm_watch.py `_queue_from` (:169-190), `take` (:209-250), `waiting` (:253-270) and the cursor/acknowledgement records all use `record_root(root)` of the firstmate session (no FM_PROJECT, so the engine), the arm's doorbell lives under the engine's state/session/wake.d, and the board's watch counter reads `ROOT/state/session/wake.jsonl` (board/server.ts:734). No waiter ever holds a doorbell under an external store (the live store's wake.d is empty), so an external wake is written where nobody reads and rings where nobody listens.

Change 1 (bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py). Add `forward(root, project, ident, reason, line)`: the one implementation that copies an external wake to the engine. It appends exactly one item to `Path(root).resolve() / WAKE_QUEUE` (the engine's own queue, never `record_root`), under the same `fcntl` exclusive append as `push`, with exactly these keys: `id` = `<project>_<ident>` (project names match `[a-z0-9-]{1,24}` and contain no `_`, so the first `_` splits it and a forwarded id can never equal a self id or another project's), `reason` = the literal `forwarded`, `origin_project` = `<project>`, `origin_reason` = the original reason, `line` = the projected line, `woken` = `time.time()`. No other field from the original item (`extra`, `decision`, `task`, `actor`, `head`, `verdict`, `rc`) is copied. The projected line is the original line with its whitespace collapsed, then, when it matches `^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z -]*): (.*)$`, `<kind>: <project> <rest>` (so `finished: T-002 worker-pilar-t002-r2 ok #1` becomes `finished: the pilot external project T-002 worker-pilar-t002-r2 ok #1` and `card: D-pilot-T002-1 answered A` becomes `card: the pilot external project D-pilot-T002-1 answered A`), else `<project>: <line>`; the result is cut to at most 300 characters. It then rings only the engine's firstmate doorbells, `_ring_directory(<engine>/state/session/wake.d, projected line)` - never `ring_state`/`ring_events`, so the engine's autopilot.d is not rung for another project's event. `forward` validates `project` against `[a-z0-9-]{1,24}` and `ident` against the existing wake-id rule (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`) and raises ValueError otherwise. It returns how many engine doorbells rang.

Change 2 (push calls forward). At the end of `push` (bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py:565-591), after the existing append and ring (both unchanged: the external store keeps its own item and rings its own wake.d exactly as today), when the resolved store is not the engine (`Path(record_root(root)).resolve() != Path(root).resolve()`) and `os.environ.get('FM_PROJECT')` is set, `push` also calls `forward(root, os.environ['FM_PROJECT'], ident, reason, line)`. A self push (record_root equals the engine) forwards nothing and writes exactly the one item it writes today. A failure inside `forward` is reported on stderr (`fm: the wake for <ident> was not forwarded to firstmate: <error>`) and never changes push's exit or its own store's write; push still returns the store's ring count. Add the CLI mode `fm_lifeline.py forward <root> <project> <id> <reason> <line>` (beside `push`, :1135-1143, and in the usage text at :53-57) that calls `forward` and prints its ring count; usage errors return `_usage()` like the other modes.

Change 3 (board/server.ts pushWake, :1565-1578). Keep the existing append into `stateDir(project)/session/wake.jsonl` and the existing `ring` call unchanged. When the card's project (`ownerOf(id)?.project ?? defaultProject()`) is a registered project whose `stateDir(project)` is not `join(ROOT, "state")`, also run `python3 LIFELINE forward ROOT <project> <id> <reason> <line>` with `stdin: "ignore"` and `childEnv()` (FM_PROJECT not set to the external project), where `<line>` is `card: <id> answered <chosen>` for `answered` (chosen from the decision record, `?` when absent) and `merge: <id> <merge>` for `merge_settled` (`settled` when absent) - the same text fm_watch.py `wake_line` (:151-166) builds for a self card. A failed spawn or non-zero exit is logged with `console.error` like the existing ring failure and never fails the answer. Self cards forward nothing.

Readers are unchanged and need no edit: fm_watch.py take/waiting/_queue_from, the acknowledgement records (fm_lifeline.py ACK_DIR), fm-session.sh status/wait, the turn-end guard and the board's watch counter (board/server.ts:734) all read the engine queue and so deliver a forwarded item like any other, by its `line` (fm_watch.py wake_line returns `line` first). The engine's autopilot reads the engine queue too (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:702-711) and acts only on `reason` `answered` and `conventions_drift`/`conventions_unknown`; a forwarded item's `reason` is `forwarded`, so the engine's autopilot never turns another project's card answer into a self `decision_made`. The project migration (bin/lib/fm_project_migrate.py:44-46) partitions records by `project` or `identity.project`; a forwarded item carries `origin_project`, not `project`, so a later `fm project sync --migrate` never moves it into a project store. Dedupe: the forwarded id is namespaced by project, so acknowledgement (keyed by id and woken) treats each forwarded wake once, and a project's own queue item is never acknowledged in the engine. In flight at deploy: wakes already sitting in an external store's queue (for example the pilot external project's T-002 items) are neither forwarded nor backfilled; only pushes after the merge are forwarded, and firstmate reads the older ones from that store's events as it does today. A tree whose `default_project` is itself external and whose firstmate session runs without FM_PROJECT reads that store, not `Path(root)`; there a forwarded item lands in the engine queue unread and does no harm - this task does not change that configuration (bin/fm-canary.sh:657 is the only such caller).

Test (fail-first; workers do not run suites; CI and the gates verify). New bash suite tests/wake-forward.test.sh, in the style of tests/project-records.test.sh:1-30 (scrub FM_/HERDR_ env, source tests/lib.sh, a temp engine with a config.yaml registering `self` (repo: .) and `private-app` (github owner/private-app), FM_HOME under the temp dir). Assertions, each red on base: (a) after `FM_PROJECT=private-app python3 bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py push "$eng" worker-x round_end 'finished: T-001 worker-x ok #1' '{"task":"T-001","actor":"worker-x","head":"abc"}'`, the store queue `$FM_HOME/projects/private-app/state/session/wake.jsonl` still has its item with `task` T-001 (unchanged behaviour) and `$eng/state/session/wake.jsonl` has exactly one item whose sorted keys are `id,line,origin_project,origin_reason,reason,woken`, with id `private-app_worker-x`, reason `forwarded`, origin_reason `round_end` and line `finished: private-app T-001 worker-x ok #1`; (b) a FIFO `$eng/state/session/wake.d/1-a.fifo` held open for reading (`exec 7<>`) receives that projected line; (c) `python3 -c` importing bin/lib/fm_watch.py with the cursor first initialised by one `take(eng)` (which returns [] and sets the cursor), then the push, then `take(eng)` returns the forwarded item and `wake_line` of it is the projected line; (d) a self push (`FM_PROJECT` unset) of id `worker-s` adds exactly one engine item, id `worker-s`, and no `forwarded` item; (e) a 400-character line is forwarded as at most 300 characters with no newline; (f) `fm_lifeline.py forward "$eng" Bad_Name x round_end l` exits non-zero and writes no engine item. Run under `set -u` with every variable before non-ASCII text braced (the suite needs none).

Existing tests that change. tests/project-records.test.sh:51-54 pushes a private wake (`FM_PROJECT=private-app ... push "$eng" D-private-app-T001-1 answered private`) and then asserts engine state holds only `dispatch.lock` (:54). Edit in place: keep :52-53; change :54 so engine state's files are exactly `dispatch.lock` and `wake.jsonl` (sorted basenames), and add that the engine queue's one item has `reason` `forwarded`, `origin_project` `private-app`, line `private-app: private` (the line `private` has no `kind: ` prefix, so Change 1 projects it as `<project>: <line>`) and none of the keys `decision`, `task`, `project`. tests/board-projects.test.sh: after the external answer at :217 (`posth D-beta-T001-1 A ...`), and after its merge settles (:218 waits for `merged`), first `wait_for 20 jq -e 'select(.reason=="forwarded" and .origin_reason=="merge_settled" and .id=="beta_D-beta-T001-1")' "$h/state/session/wake.jsonl"` (the board writes `merged` to the record at server.ts:1641-1644 before pushWake at :1653 forwards, so the record alone is not enough), then add assertions that `$h/state/session/wake.jsonl` has exactly one `forwarded` item with id `beta_D-beta-T001-1` and line `card: beta D-beta-T001-1 answered A` (origin_reason `answered`), and exactly one with the same id and line `merge: beta D-beta-T001-1 merged` (origin_reason `merge_settled`) - two items, one per wake, as the self card D-51 gets two queue items in tests/board-wake.test.sh - and that no `forwarded` item has an id beginning `alpha_` (the self answer at :198 forwards nothing). tests/board-wake.test.sh (self cards D-51..D-53), tests/watch.test.sh, tests/session.test.sh, tests/decide.test.sh, tests/emit.test.sh, tests/review-verdict.test.sh, tests/worker-exits.test.sh, tests/conventions-watch.test.sh, tests/board-state.test.sh, tests/lib/autopilot_startup_cache.py, tests/lib/preflight_lifecycle.py, tests/herdr/agentlost.py:25-34 (self lost wake, exact queue contents) and tests/lib/merge_board_binding.py (self settlement doorbell wait) (every file `grep -ln 'wake.jsonl\|lifeline.py" push\|fm_wake'` lists) push or read only self wakes or migrate fixture items without `origin_project`; none of their assertions changes. Check each and state it in the PR. tests/project-migration.test.sh: edit in place at :35 - add a third fixture line to the engine wake queue, `{"id":"private-app_worker-x","reason":"forwarded","origin_project":"private-app","origin_reason":"round_end","line":"finished: private-app T-001 worker-x ok"}` - and at :56-57 assert the migrated project queue still holds only `private wake` and the engine queue holds the `self wake` line and the forwarded line (two lines, the forwarded id unchanged), so migration never moves a forwarded item. Autopilot guard: add case `forwarded_wake_is_not_a_decision` to tests/lib/autopilot_startup_cache.py (same setUp; saved zero cursors as in test_saved_zero_cursors_resume_instead_of_skipping_unread_events, :99-107; write only one wake row `{"id":"private-app_D-private-app-T001-1","reason":"forwarded","origin_reason":"answered","origin_project":"private-app","line":"card: private-app D-private-app-T001-1 answered A"}` and no event row; `A.Pilot(self.ctx).local()`; assert `pilot.data['wakes'] == {}`) and list it in tests/autopilot-startup-cache.test.sh's case loop. It is a guard: green on base by design, it pins that the engine autopilot never turns another project's answer into a self decision.

Callers checked (grep `life.push\|lifeline().push\|fm_wake_push\|pushWake` in bin/ and board/): bin/fm-config.sh:894 fm_wake_push, used by bin/fm-worker.sh:364 and bin/fm-review.sh:251; bin/fm-herdr.py:1964 (lost); bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:123; bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:96; bin/lib/fm_watch.py:386 (the conventions tick inside the watch passes life.push; it resolves against the watch's own environment, where FM_PROJECT is unset, so it forwards nothing); bin/fm-emit.sh:290-300 wake_on_gate (calls `fm_lifeline.py push "$ROOT" ...` directly at :298, so an external gate result emitted with FM_PROJECT set is forwarded too); board/server.ts:1565 pushWake, called at :1653 (merge settled) and :2295 (answered). All reach the change through `push` or pushWake; none of their signatures changes.

Design (edit in place, no new section at the end, T-189). design/design.md §11 Self-update, '### Owners and wakes (T-151)' (design.md:2743), paragraph '*Waking the harness (T-137).*' (design.md:2854-2868): add, after the list of writers, that a wake pushed into an external project's store is also forwarded to the engine queue as one bounded item (`reason` `forwarded`, `origin_project`, `origin_reason`, the line naming the project) and rung on the engine's doorbells only, so one watch hears every project. §15.3 (design.md:4916-4922): after 'never written into engine state or public diagrams', add the one exception: the forwarded wake item, which carries only its namespaced id, reason, origin project and reason, the projected line and the time. §15.8 (design.md:5390-5391, 'External records and FIFOs live only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/state/'): state the same exception for the forwarded wake line.

Out of scope: the watch cycle, the arm, the guard and the hook entries (bin/lib/fm_watch.py, bin/fm-watch*.sh, bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh, bin/lib/fm_hooks.py); the board's watch counter; the autopilot; the external store's own queue and doorbells (kept as they are); any per-project cursor or multi-store reader; the content of any line a writer builds.
